scenes.title: Cold open
narration: The God Who Lying in Fire Defied Caste
This is Pottan Theyyam. Pre-modern to contemporary.
on_screen: Title card: Pottan Theyyam · India · Pre-modern to contemporary

scenes.title: Where and when
narration: Pottan Theyyam originated in Kolathunadu, an area encompassing Kannur district and parts of Kozhikode and Kasaragod districts in northern Kerala.
Formed within the Theyyam tradition, it emerged as an anti-caste ritual that re-enacts the lives of those who sacrificed their lives challenging social oppression.
In local narrative, the dance is based on an encounter where a Dalit figure challenged Shankaracharya's enforcement of caste pollution on a public path.

scenes.title: When it is danced
narration: Performed as a Theyyam sacred festival rite symbolizing resistance against caste injustice and social evils.
It represents an anti-caste god and serves as a vehicle through which marginalized history speaks directly to society.
Today it is a living tradition.

scenes.title: Watch it
narration: The performance combines ritual movement, spoken satire, and dramatic confrontation.
A core physical feature is the deity lying directly upon the glowing embers of a large ritual bonfire.
The gathered community repeatedly implores the performer to get up from the fire.
Watch for Resting on embers, Dialogue of equality.

scenes.title: The people
narration: The legend centers on Pottan, an anti-caste deity considered a manifestation of Shiva, and the Advaita philosopher Adi Shankaracharya whom Pottan confronted.
A branch of the living Theyyam ritual art form preserved within the regional heritage of Kolathunadu, northern Kerala.

scenes.title: A respectful note
narration: Pottan Theyyam is an anti-caste ritual deity manifestation performed in sacred tharavad shrines (palliyara) and temple grounds. The performer enters an altered state to embody Shiva and communally dialogue with devotees. outsiders should maintain reverence, avoid trespassing on sacred pyres, and not mimic the ritual actions outside traditional cultural contexts.

images.description: Pottan Theyyam is a vivid, lively and colorful ritualistic dance which comes in the traditional art form of theyyam, and is an essential part of the cultural heritage of Kolathunadu, a territory comprising the present Kannur district and parts of Calicut and Kasargod districts of Kerala, India.
